transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-10-07 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~45 mins
- Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Leah Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Menon (FoldLabs ML Eng), Tom Sawyer (FoldLabs Product), Elena Baca (FoldLabs DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, brief):
Redwood + FoldLabs week 4 POC sync focused on cache hit-rate behavior. Current KV hit-rate low (~28% reported) with prefix cache ~41%. Discussed prompt canonicalization, prompt reuse, TTL/eviction tuning, prefetch patterns, and measurement instrumentation. Agreed next steps: KV sweep, logs export, pricing send, canary plan.

Topics covered:
- Current hit-rate numbers and measurement sanity checks
- Prompt variation and normalization approach
- Eviction/TTL and prefetch tuning tradeoffs
- Metrics to watch (p50/p95 latency, token cost, GPU utilization)
- Rollout plan and safety/fallbacks

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can kick off, um, high level quick check, agenda is hit-rate review and tuning plan
[01:05] Priya Menon: thanks, yeah we wanted to see the week over week numbers, we've been seeing... like a big gap between expected and actual KV hits
[02:12] Marco Ruiz: right, so per our dashboard the KV hit is hovering at ~28% across the last 72 hours, prefix cache is around 41%. i want to call out those numbers are on the raw logs so there could be some normalization artifacts
[03:01] Tom Sawyer: when you say "normalization artifacts" what do you mean? are prompts being hashed differently or is it whitespace / user tokens?
[03:15] Marco Ruiz: both. we're seeing a lot of surface-level diffs: timestamps in prompts, session IDs, slight ordering differences of bullets. those make near-duplicate prompts look unique to the cache key generator
[04:07] Priya Menon: yep that's exactly what we thought. our prompt templates have user metadata inserted and sometimes optional fields are present or not.
[05:00] Avery Chen: do you have an example of a high-volume prompt that we can canonicalize?
[05:24] Priya Menon: yes, the "summary + actions" template, it's used for ~30% of calls but the top three variants change insertion order, sometimes they include debug flags
[06:10] Marco Ruiz: ok if we canonicalize—that is strip debug flags, normalize whitespace, and reorder structured sections—hit-rate should increase. quick sanity math: if that template is 30% of traffic and canonicalization groups 80% of its variants we could get ~24% absolute hit bump, which would push overall KV hit to the mid-50s potentially
[07:22] Elena Baca: mid-50s would be great — how does that affect latency? we want to ensure p95 doesn't spike during cache misses
[08:14] Marco Ruiz: good question. caching primarily reduces token generation cost and p50 latency — for p95 we rely on fast fallback and batching. we do continuous batching on the runtime; when hit-rate increases you see a small p50 improvement and p95 is stable unless backend GPU queueing changes
[09:01] Tom Sawyer: are we seeing any queuing issues today?
[09:30] Marco Ruiz: not at RL scale, GPU utilization is at ~60% for the pilot cluster, tail latency occasionally bumps during big bursts but nothing sustained. those bursts correspond to non-cacheable prompts from a small set of users
[10:22] Priya Menon: curious about prefix cache vs KV: what's the recommended split? currently we have prefix enabled for a subset of templates, KV for the rest
[11:05] Marco Ruiz: prefix cache is best when the same token prefix repeats across sessions, KV is better for full prompt reuse. combination is common: prefix for the first 256 tokens and KV for entire canonical prompts. we'd recommend enabling both for high-volume templates, then measure overlap
[12:11] Avery Chen: on the pilot config we can flip on a more aggressive prefix TTL, but note TTL trades off staleness — if your templates change you'd want a shorter TTL or eviction on model rollout
[13:00] Elena Baca: ok what TTLs are typical? minutes, hours?
[13:18] Marco Ruiz: depends — for near-production e2e, 30m to 2h is common for prefix. KV entries for canonicalized prompts can be longer, like 6-24h, but that's workload dependent and also tied to content-sensitivity for compliance
[14:00] Priya Menon: about compliance — would longer KV entries be a problem for data retention? we need to keep to our retention policy and make sure logs are deletable
[14:25] Avery Chen: good flag — Redwood supports TTL-based purging and we can scopingtion the KMS/SSE policies. we'll include guidance in the security docs; Leah, can you attach the retention controls doc to the follow-up?
[14:48] Leah Patel: yeah i'll add that to the follow-up email, short note and link to the controls page
[15:40] Marco Ruiz: another lever is prompt shingling / fingerprinting—if we take N-gram shingles of the prompt and use a fuzzy match threshold we can bucket near-duplicates. that helps when small diffs like punctuation occur
[16:32] Priya Menon: sounds promising. what's the runtime cost of fuzzy matching?
[16:58] Marco Ruiz: it's small if done at the pre-processing layer and batched. we can run it in a lightweight lambda or in our fronting service; cost is negligible compared to model inference costs but it adds a small CPU preproc step
[17:45] Tom Sawyer: and how do we measure the improvement? what's the instrumentation we should expect in the dashboard?
[18:12] Marco Ruiz: great point — we have a cache-hitrate dashboard (link: https://redwood.example/cache-hitrate/foldlabs) that shows per-template KV/prefix hit, per-route p50/p95 latency, tokens saved, and estimated token cost savings. we'll add a per-template canonicalization metric after Marco's sweep
[19:25] Priya Menon: can we also get a breakdown by user segment? mobile vs web? our behavior differs
[19:52] Marco Ruiz: yes we can split the metrics. the FoldLabs logs include client tags so we'll surface that in the dashboard once logs are ingested
[20:40] Avery Chen: on the KV sweep Marco, what parameters will you vary?
[20:53] Marco Ruiz: i'll vary canonicalization rules (strip debug flags, timestamp masking, order canonicalization), and also try shingling thresholds 0.8 and 0.9, plus a quick experiment with longer KV TTL (24h vs 6h) to see storage hit vs reuse
[21:30] Elena Baca: storage — will costs go up with 24h TTLs? we are cost-sensitive in the pilot
[21:50] Marco Ruiz: storage cost is small relative to token compute, but it scales linearly with unique keys and TTL. part of the sweep is to provide an estimated cost delta so you can weigh it against saved token spend
[22:35] Tom Sawyer: anything we need to change client-side? we have a cached local layer in the app right now
[22:48] Priya Menon: we do, but it's rudimentary — mostly response-level caching. we'd prefer the server-side approach if Redwood can guarantee consistent gains
[23:30] Marco Ruiz: server-side is better for cross-client dedupe. apps can continue local cache for ultra-low-latency cases but server-side KV gives global reuse, which is what will move the needle for cost
[24:12] Avery Chen: quick note on rollout safety: we'll do canary for prefix TTL and canonicalization in parallel. if bit flips cause regressions we auto-fallback to baseline model variant as configured in your rollout policy
[24:56] Leah Patel: i'll add canary success criteria: no >5% increase in p95 and >=10% token cost reduction in the canary group within 24h of the change
[25:38] Priya Menon: are there any gotchas with quantization or model variants? we sometimes route to smaller quantized forks for low-cost mode
[25:58] Marco Ruiz: quantized models generally behave same for caching. but if output changes meaningfully you might see cache mismatch; therefore tie cache keys to model variant id so different model outputs don't collide
[26:40] Tom Sawyer: on the docs — can you share the canonicalization rules repo or a gist?
[26:57] Marco Ruiz: yes i'll push a gist and the python preproc script, link in the follow-up (we'll call it canonicalize.py). will include unit tests for common template cases
[27:30] Priya Menon: timeline question — after you run the sweep, how long until we can see stable numbers?
[27:46] Marco Ruiz: sweep results should be in 48–72h. then we can apply a canary which will run for 24–48h. so rough timeline is 1–2 weeks to get to a stable config for high-volume templates
[28:30] Elena Baca: ok does Redwood need infra changes on our side for the sweep?
[28:45] Marco Ruiz: mainly the 72h logs export that Priya will share. otherwise we can run preproc and experiments from our side. if we need to change routing or model variants for the canary we'll coordinate a short maintenance window but typically no infra changes required
[29:30] Priya Menon: re: logs — can we redact PII automatically? we have to ensure anonymization before sharing
[29:50] Avery Chen: absolutely — we have a log-scrub template. Priya, if you run the scrub locally and then share the S3 link with read-only access that's fine
[30:30] Tom Sawyer: ok i also want to revisit cost modeling for dedicated capacity — last time you showed a per-million-token delta, can we get a refreshed calc with our projected QPS?
[30:50] Avery Chen: yes i'll refresh the cost model with your projected QPS numbers; send those latest forecasts as a sheet and i'll slot them in
[31:32] Priya Menon: quick note — some prompts are session-specific and can't be cached; we need a list of non-cacheable patterns so we can avoid wasted work
[31:50] Marco Ruiz: we'll generate a "do-not-cache" pattern list based on regexes and token markers; we'll include that as a PR to the canonicalization rules
[32:30] Elena Baca: any impact to our SLOs? we're tracking 99.9 up time and latency SLOs in our infra
[32:45] Leah Patel: from Redwood side the pilot SLA is informational; for production Dedicated we can discuss formal SLAs. For pilot changes we'll ensure no change to core availability guarantees
[33:30] Tom Sawyer: can we see sample traces of a cache hit vs miss in the dashboard? that helps debug
[33:45] Marco Ruiz: yes there's a trace view, we will enable sample trace capture for the canary group so you can inspect p95 tails and spot correlated infra events
[34:20] Priya Menon: about prefetching — you mentioned earlier a prefetch strategy for likely next prompts, can you explain?
[34:40] Marco Ruiz: prefetch is speculative: if your app has predictable step sequences we can precompute the next likely prompt and warm the KV/prefix cache. it increases requests slightly but reduces perceived latency for the next call
[35:20] Tom Sawyer: sounds risky — more requests mean more cost
[35:35] Marco Ruiz: yes, so we only recommend prefetch where the probability of the next prompt > threshold (e.g., 70%) and we cap prefetch window to top-N for each session to limit cost
[36:15] Priya Menon: can we do A/B testing for prefetch?
[36:30] Avery Chen: yes we can run A/B with canary flags and measure net token spend vs latency gains. Leah will help instrument the experiment in Console
[37:10] Leah Patel: i'll add experiment dashboard to the follow-up and include sample visualizations for cost vs latency tradeoff
[37:55] Marco Ruiz: on instrumentation I'll also push a small sample harness so you can reproduce the measurement locally if helpful
[38:20] Priya Menon: perfect — last Q: are there known regressions with function calling / streaming? we use streaming a bit for progressive results
[38:43] Marco Ruiz: streaming can complicate prefix caching because partial outputs are different each call. caching is best for final, deterministic responses. for streaming we rely more on prefix and smaller prefix TTLs
[39:30] Tom Sawyer: ok wrapping up, what's the single biggest lift we should expect from canonicalization?
[39:45] Marco Ruiz: canonicalization plus shingling should be the quickest win — probably a 20–35 percentage point lift on templates that are high-variance today, end-to-end lift depends on distribution but likely moves overall from ~28% to 50–60% if most high-volume templates are covered
[40:30] Priya Menon: that would be a huge cost saver for us. we'll prioritize exporting logs and the top templates this week
[41:10] Avery Chen: great. i'll recap next steps in email. Leah will send calendar invite for canary slot. Marco will start the sweep once logs land.
[42:00] Leah Patel: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the retention docs and the canary invite
[42:30] Priya Menon: thanks all
[42:40] Tom Sawyer: thanks
[42:45] Marco Ruiz: thanks, talk soon
